item.title: Austin Championship: Trace Crowe grabs 54-hole lead late
item.description: Trace Crowe birdied his final two holes Saturday to get to 14 under and separate himself from three other players through 54 holes of the inaugural Austin Championship . Chad Ramey, Erik van Rooyen and Sami Valimaki all could have shared the lead heading into Sunday's final round at Fazio Canyons Golf Course if Crowe had faltered down the stretch. But the 30-year-old Crowe, who is seeking his first win on Tour this week in Texas, birdied the par-3 17th and followed it up with another circle at No. 18 as part of the final grouping on the course. "It was like 220 straight into the wind, I was just trying to hit a 4-iron as low as I could and push it just a touch," Crowe recalled. "It was actually a pretty good shot to end up in that bunker, it was a good leave. He called the lie perfect as it was just sitting uphill. "It just came out perfect and went in — me and my caddie both had a feeling I was going to make that before we got it, so it was pretty cool to see that go in," he added. Heavy winds began to impact players still on their back nines Saturday afternoon, and Crowe was no exception. After setting the course record on Thursday with an opening-round 62, Crowe bogeyed the first two holes on his back nine on Moving Day. Another square at the par-4 16th put his chances in doubt but the run of birdies at the end of his round vaulted him ahead for the solo lead. Americans Ben Kohles and Max Greyserman are two back of Crowe's lead, while eight players sit T-7 at 11 under. Ramey had the clubhouse lead for more than an hour. He got there by limiting mistakes — the 34-year-old Mississippi State alum has posted just three bogeys, one in each round. Saturday's error came at the par-3 17th, the same hole Crowe birdied from an hour later. "On a week like this to kind of finally get some good results and be in a good position going into Sunday, it's great to see," said Ramey, who entered the week No. 136 in the FedExCup Fall standings and has moved up to a projected No. 68. Austin Championship - Final Rd The Austin Championship tees off at Omni Barton Creek Resort & Spa in Austin, Texas. That would give Ramey a card for 2027, despite not having a top 10 finish in his first 26 starts. Valimaki, who won for the first time at the RSM Classic last November , moved into the co-leader position with a 3-under 69. He opened the inaugural tournament 68-66 after making his first PGA Tour start since July at last week's WWT Championship. "It was good to take some time off, it's actually been a long time since I felt like I could enjoy the golf course and I feel like that's the biggest key for me," said Valimaki, who battled a right wrist injury and also received stiches in his left hand. The Finnish player was No. 172 entering the week but has crept up to No. 129 with 18 holes left. The top 100 players earn their cards , while players inside the top 125 earn conditional status for the 2027 season. Van Rooyen was more up and down with his 69 on Saturday. He bogeyed

item.title: Smyth scores 55-yard field goal in Saints defeat
item.description: Smyth was making his second NFL appearance of the season against the Panthers [Getty Images] Kicker Charlie Smyth landed a late 55-yard field goal, but it wasn't enough to stop New Orleans Saints falling to a 20-17 defeat against Carolina Panthers on Sunday. The former Gaelic footballer, from Mayobridge in County Down, was making his second NFL appearance of the season after being elevated from the practice squad for a second successive week. The 25-year-old helped the Saints to an overtime win against Cleveland Browns last weekend with three field goals and two extra points and he was almost the hero again against the Panthers. Smyth, who also kicked two extra points, landed a 55-yard field goal with just 41 seconds left in regulation time to tie the game at 17-17. However, Panthers quarterback Bryce Young's drive set up Panthers' kicker Ryan Fitzgerald to score a 54-yard field goal on the final play to win the game.

item.title: ‘Hitting the Powerball’… Kansas City Chiefs star has never had it so good, says Ryan Clark
item.description: Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs’ newest receiving weapon showed up immediately against the Atlanta Falcons. Chiefs general manager Brett Veach provided a surprise for quarterback Patrick Mahomes at the NFL trade deadline, agreeing a trade for Josh Downs. Downs was traded away by the Indianapolis Colts to the Chiefs for a fourth and fifth round pick, a move that could end up looking like a bargain. The new Kansas City Chiefs wide receiver made an instant impact in Week 10 in his first game for his new team. Downs caught his first touchdown from Patrick Mahomes in the second quarter, catching an 18-yard pass in the endzone. NFL expert Ryan Clark reacted to Downs’ first Chiefs touchdown by reflecting on the incredible turnaround in fortunes for the receiver – after leaving the 2-7 Colts. Clark posted on social media: “Man, imagine going to sleep one week with Daniel Jones as your QB, and waking up the next with Patrick Mahomes! “That’s the football version of hitting the Powerball! I know Josh Downs feels like a new man!” Downs leaves a losing team for a winning team Josh Downs had requested a trade away from the Indianapolis Colts after their poor start to the season, and clear intention to rebuild. His Colts team were 2-7 heading into Week 10, while the Chiefs were 6-2 prior to their win over the Falcons. Downs has never played a game in the NFL Playoffs during his three seasons in Indianapolis. Now providing he can stay injury-free in Kansas City, Downs will likely finally get the chance to play in the postseason with the Chiefs. It’s hard to disagree with Ryan Clark’s assessment that he has ‘won the Powerball’ with the trade. item.title: Inside New Chiefs Acquisition Josh Downs’ Debut Vs. Falcons
item.description: Josh Downs of the Kansas City Chiefs makes a catch for a touchdown against Billy Bowman Jr. (No. 33) of the Atlanta Falcons during the second quarter at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on Nov. 15, 2026. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs wasted no time in unwrapping their new toy. Wide receiver Josh Downs, who the Chiefs acquired from the Indianapolis Colts for 2027 fourth- and fifth-round picks on Tuesday, was involved early in Sunday’s 35-13 victory at the Atlanta Falcons. Downs, who had four catches for 51 yards and a touchdown, played in every drive of the first quarter, but it was on special teams where he first saw action. After the Falcons went three-and-out on the game’s opening series, Downs was back to return the punt, though it ended up being a touchback. He was the returner on all three of the Chiefs’ punt returns. In the second quarter, Downs really picked up steam on the offensive side. On the Chiefs’ last drive of the first half, Chiefs kicker Harrison Butker kicked a 41-yard field goal, but the Falcons jumped offside on fourth down, giving the Chiefs a first down and another offensive opportunity. It turned out to be a costly mistake for the Falcons, which would change the game. Lined up with two other wide receivers on the left side, Downs ran an option route, which is one of his specialties, and Patrick Mahomes showed faith in him despite double coverage from defensive backs Billy Bowman Jr. and C.J. Henderson. The result was an 18-yard touchdown . “That’s a trust play,” Chiefs head coach Andy Reid said. Two offensive plays before his first touchdown as a Chiefs player, Downs was targeted on consecutive plays, which resulted in a 13-yard catch and then an incompletion. Downs’ lone downside — lame pun intended — came on the Chiefs’ second punt return when he fumbled the 50-yard punt, forcing the Chiefs to start their possession on their own four-yard line. The Chiefs did have some special teams gaffes, including allowing an onside kick to be converted, but Downs was part of a prolific, downfield Chiefs passing game. Mahomes completed 22-of-35 passes for 348 yards and five touchdowns. “Pat had a huge day,” Reid said, “and was slinging it.” Backup wide receiver Andrew Armstrong scored a 43-yard touchdown on 3rd and 1. Mahomes connected with receiver Rashee Rice who had a 50-yard contested catch for the longest gain of the game. Rice and Downs have their own connection, having trained together in the offseason and coming out of college. “That’s my dog,” Downs said. The Chiefs knew they were getting a dog in Downs after seeing him lead the Colts with seven catches for 72 yards during the Colts’ overtime loss to Kansas City in Week Two. “We saw that firsthand,” Reid said. “I had to watch him live, which wasn’t good.” Further confirmation came from conversations with Chris Ballard, who the Colts fired as general manager earlier this year. item.title: Chiefs thrash Falcons as Mahomes throws five touchdowns
item.description: Patrick Mahomes was back to his imperious best, completing 22-of 35 passes with zero interceptions and one sack in a win that took the Kansas City Chiefs level with the idle Denver Broncos top of the AFC West (Todd Kirkland) Patrick Mahomes threw for five touchdowns and 348 yards as the Kansas City Chiefs thrashed the Falcons 35-13 at Atlanta on Sunday. Mahomes was back to his imperious best, completing 22-of-35 passes with zero interceptions and one sack in a win that took the Chiefs level with the idle Denver Broncos top of the AFC West. Rookie Emmett Johnson twice found the end zone, while Josh Downs had a touchdown on his Kansas City debut following a deadline day trade from Indianapolis. Cyrus Allen and Andrew Armstrong each scored their first Chiefs touchdowns, grabbing passes of 39 yards and 43 yards respectively as Mahomes dominated the Falcons defense. It was the three-time Super Bowl champion quarterback's most impressive showing since his nine-month injury absence after tearing his knee ligaments last December. "Guys made plays, you know? I gave them chances downfield, and they went out there and made plays happen," said Mahomes. Johnson -- stepping up for Kenneth Walker III, who was absent with a groin injury -- also led the Chiefs' running game, with 22 carries for 101 yards. Star tight end Travis Kelce left the field early, injuring his ankle as he was tackled taking his first catch, but returned in the second quarter. "I thought we did a great job picking up, obviously Kenneth not being here. I thought Emmett did a great job, and then the O-line gave me chances to throw the ball down the field," said Mahomes. It was another miserable day for the Falcons, who trailed 28-3 before Bijan Robinson's fourth-quarter touchdown, and have now lost three straight and five of their past six. Elsewhere, the Cleveland Browns rallied from 17-0 down to stun the Houston Texans 27-24, as Quinshon Judkins ran in a touchdown with less than a minute remaining. The Texans had led with C.J. Stroud's first-half passing touchdowns to Nico Collins and Xavier Hutchinson. The Browns fought back to take the lead with touchdowns either side of halftime, from a Deshaun Watson six-yard run, a KC Concepcion rushing touchdown and two field goals, all without reply. The Texans thought they had salvaged the win with a Stroud pass to Dalton Schultz, before Watson led yet another late game-winning drive and Judkins ran five yards for the win with 53 seconds left. "It was definitely a big win for us overall, but personally for me it was definitely special," said Watson, who was drafted by the Texans in 2017 and traded to Cleveland five years later. - 'Tough three years' - Kirk Cousins threw for two touchdowns even as he was sacked three times on his return to the Minnesota Vikings, who beat divisional rivals Green Bay 30-10 on Sunday. item.title: Andreeva defeats Svitolina to win WTA Finals
item.description: Russian teenager Mirra Andreeva celebrates victory over Elina Svitolina in the WTA Finals in Indian Wells (MATTHEW STOCKMAN) Russian teenager Mirra Andreeva battled past Elina Svitolina in straight sets to win the season-ending WTA Finals crown on Sunday. Andreeva powered to a 7-5, 6-3 victory in a hard-fought duel in Indian Wells to complete a superb week in California. Reigning French Open champion Andreeva, 19, clinched the title without dropping a set in the tournament. She is only the third teenager after Chris Evert and Maria Sharapova to win the WTA Finals on their debut. "It feels amazing, of course I'm super-privileged to put my name in that group," said Andreeva. The teenager thanked friends, family and support staff in a victory speech, before light-heartedly thanking herself for her success. "I want to thank myself for always doing the hard work, for never quitting, for always believing in myself, for not taking the days off, for working every day, and for committing to what I have to do," said Andreeva, wearing a track-suit top with the slogan "I want to thank myself." A grueling 1hr 48min duel saw Andreeva secure a break in the opening game of the first set before holding for a 2-0 lead. Ukrainian veteran Svitolina broke back in the fourth game, conjuring a sublime angled volley to level at 2-2. Svitolina was soon back under pressure though, conceding another break to go 4-3 down before Andreeva held for a 5-3 lead. There was more drama to follow when Andreeva served for the first set at 5-4 up. She opened with back-to-back double faults to go 0-30 down, and then yanked a wild forehand wide to give Svitolina two break points at 15-40. A long forehand gave Svitolina the break to knot it at 5-5 but Andreeva hit back immediately with her third break of serve to regain the advantage at 6-5. The Russian made no mistake when serving for the set for a second time, holding comfortably to go 1-0 up. The second set followed a familiar pattern, with both players trading some brutal groundstrokes in a series of long rallies. Andreeva broke to take the lead at 1-0 but Svitolina responded in a marathon second game, breaking back after converting her seventh break point to level at 1-1. Andreeva edged back in front with a break to go 3-2 up and then held for a 4-2 lead. The next two games went with serve to leave Svitolina serving to stay in the match at 5-3 down. A fortunate net cord left Andreeva with three match points at 0-40. Svitolina saved the first and looked poised to save another, only to hit a wide open overhead smash into the net to give Andreeva the win. Svitolina, who had been thumped 6-4, 6-0 by Andreeva in the opening round-robin game of the tournament, took positives from her performance. "After the first match I was not expecting to play in the final," Svitolina said. "Unfortunately it didn't go my way but I gave it my all." rcw/amz

item.title: ‘So Happy for Him,’ ‘He’s What We Needed’ — NFL Fans React to Kirk Cousins Getting Emotional After Leading Minnesota to Huge Win vs. Packers
item.description: ‘So Happy for Him,’ ‘He’s What We Needed’ — NFL Fans React to Kirk Cousins Getting Emotional After Leading Minnesota to Huge Win vs. Packers Kirk Cousins had plenty of reasons to enjoy beating Green Bay, but getting through the postgame interview proved a little harder. Back in a Vikings uniform at the stadium where his first stint with Minnesota ended, Cousins became emotional discussing the road that brought him back. Fans who watched the moment were ready to welcome him home, even if this particular reunion happened on enemy territory. Kirk Cousins’ Return Hits Home With Vikings Fans Minnesota defeated the Packers 30-10 at Lambeau Field on Sunday, with Cousins completing 21 of 31 passes for 207 yards, two touchdowns, and an interception. The victory pushed the Vikings to 7-2 and completed a season sweep of their division rival. The significance went well beyond another win in the standings. Cousins suffered his season-ending Achilles injury at Lambeau in October 2023, during what became the final game of his first Minnesota tenure. Returning there in purple and gold brought those memories back. “I tore my Achilles here and it’s been a tough three years,” Cousins said in an emotional interview shared by ESPN’s Lindsey Thiry . Welcome home!” the fan wrote . Another supporter had already seen enough to endorse the reunion. “SKOL!!💛🏈💜So great to see him back, he’s what we needed!!!” the fan wrote . “Good for him!” another fan added . SET YOUR LINEUPS: PFN’s Free Fantasy Start/Sit Optimizer There is a pretty good recipe for winning over Minnesota fans. Put on the purple, beat the Packers, and give everyone a reason to feel something afterward. Cousins checked every box on Sunday. Cousins Gives Minnesota an Encouraging First Chapter The Vikings reacquired Cousins from the Raiders for a 2027 third-round pick at the trade deadline. That left him only a handful of days to prepare for his first start back with the organization. He now ranks ninth with a PFN QB Impact Score of 80.7 across his 10 appearances this season. Sunday provided an encouraging opening to the Minnesota portion of that campaign. The affection in the replies was just as obvious. “Kirko forever on lovewatch man🥹,” one fan wrote . “I love this guy,” another added . “So proud of you,” another supporter wrote . item.title: Cucurella and Huijsen feature as Spain surrender Nations League group lead to England
item.description: MADRID, SPAIN - NOVEMBER 15: Jude Bellingham of England gestures towards Marc Cucurella of Spain during the UEFA Nations League 2026/27 group phase match between Spain and England at Riyadh Air Metropolitano on November 15, 2026 in Madrid, Spain. (Photo by Carl Recine/Getty Images) | Getty Images There was a party atmosphere at a sold-out Metropolitano on Sunday night as Spain hosted England in their first game in the Spanish capital since conquering the World Cup in the summer. Luis de la Fuente’s side had won five from five in the UEFA Nations League campaign and were unbeaten in 90 minutes in 43 games, since March 2024, with this expected to see them crowned as group winners in the UEFA Nations League. Instead, England ran out the winners, taking a 3-0 lead through a Harry Kane penalty, an Ezri Konsa header and a third from Ben White. Spain did battle back to 3-2 after the Three Lions went down to 10 men after Elliot Anderson was sent off for fouling Lamine Yamal in the box, with Mikel Oyarzabal scoring the resulting penalty and Nico Williams adding another. At left-back, Marc Cucurella had a night to forget. Booked for a foul on Morgan Rogers early in the second half, he won only one of five ground duels and didn’t complete any tackles as he struggled with the threat of Rogers down England’s right flank. Going forwards, he also contributed little with only two passes into the final third and failing to find his target with his only attempted cross. In the second half, he was joined by Dean Huijsen, who came on at the break to replace Pau Cubarsí, who conceded the penalty which gave England the lead before half-time. Huijsen too found it hard going up against Kane, losing all four of his aerial duels, and also failing to complete any tackles. Where he did contribute more was in Spain’s more direct approach with Huijsen often carrying the ball forwards before launching it into the final third later on, registering six passes into the final third and a step by 92% pass accuracy overall. Spain have now finished second in the group, behind England on goal difference, which means that they will face a tougher draw in the Nations League play-off before a final four.

item.title: The full Division III football bracket, along with at least 1 major snub
item.description: The transition from a selection committee to the NCAA Power Index (NPI) has taken some of the guess work from the Division III football championship bracket. The expansion from 32 teams to 40 has ensured fewer snubs. But that doesn't mean this year's field doesn't bring surprises. Geographic limitations and the NPI's difference of opinion with the D3Football.com rankings means there's plenty to quibble about with this year's schedule. Wheaton College, the first team to beat powerhouse North Central in the regular season since 2019, went from the poll's No. 1 team to the bracket's third overall seed. Wisconsin-Whitewater, chasing its first national title since 2014, will have home field advantage all the way to the national championship game in Salem, Virginia after topping out the NPI formula. Teams with solid resumes, like Bethel and reigning national champion Wisconsin-River Falls, were left out. The New England Small College Athletic Conference (NESCAC) put three teams in the bracket even though the league didn't play a single out-of-conference game . North Central and DePauw, each ranked in the poll's top 15, will face off in a second round game that ensures at least one realistic title contender will be gone before the field is whittled down to 16 teams. You can find the full bracket here . Or expand the image below. The tournament begins November 21. The national title will be decided, on January 3, on ESPN. This article originally appeared on For The Win: The full Division III football bracket, along with at least 1 major snub

item.title: Raiders’ Fernando Mendoza on board with TD vs. Seahawks that’s a throwback to Indiana’s national championship game
item.description: Christopher Trim-Imagn Images Raiders’ Fernando Mendoza on board with TD vs. Seahawks that’s a throwback to Indiana’s national championship game appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . On Sunday afternoon, the Las Vegas Raiders hit the field at home for a game vs the Seattle Seahawks. This game marked the first start for quarterback Fernando Mendoza , who took over after the Raiders traded Kirk Cousins to the Minnesota Vikings last week. While there was plenty of doubt about Mendoza making his first start against the vaunted Seahawks’ defense, he answered the call early on in this one, leading the Raiders on a march down the field and ultimately punching the ball into the end zone with an impressive run. FERNANDO MENDOZA . FIRST START, FIRST TD RUN 🙌 pic.twitter.com/8LNpsESc1U Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) November 15, 2026 The play reminded some of the 2025-26 college football national championship game, in which Mendoza made a Herculean run to help the Indiana Hoosiers knock off the Miami Hurricanes for their first national title in school history. While he is typically viewed as more of a traditional pocket passer, Mendoza has shown an ability and willingness to use his legs to make plays dating back to his college days, and he wasted no time in establishing that he can still do that at the NFL level, against one of the league’s top defensive units at that. There will inevitably be growing pains for Mendoza as he adjusts to the NFL level, but hopefully his strong start early on against the Seahawks will give fans enough evidence to not get restless whenever mistakes do occur. In any case, at the conclusion of the Seahawks game, the Raiders will next hit the field next week for a tough road game against the Denver Broncos. item.title: England player ratings vs Spain: Harry Kane leads clinical victory to secure top spot
item.description: FBL-EUR-NATIONS-ESP-ENG - AFP England secured a dramatic 3-2 victory over Spain at the Riyadh Air Metropolitano to clinch top spot in Nations League Group A3. Goals from Harry Kane, Ezri Konsa, and Ben White built a commanding lead that withstood a late Spanish fightback. England delivered a tactical masterclass in efficiency to overcome Spain in a five-goal thriller at the Riyadh Air Metropolitano. Despite ceding 64% of possession to Luis de la Fuente’s side, the Three Lions were devastating in transitional moments and set-piece scenarios. Kane’s clinical penalty just before the interval set the tone, before a rapid-fire double early in the second half stunned the hosts and ended their long unbeaten run. The defensive resolve of Thomas Tuchel’s side was tested severely in the closing stages as Spain mounted a spirited comeback through Mikel Oyarzabal and Nico Williams. However, England’s ability to convert three of their five shots on target proved the difference. This result ensures England leapfrog Spain to finish first in Group 3, showcasing a pragmatic edge that bodes well for the upcoming tournament cycles under Tuchel’s stewardship. Goalkeeper & Defence James Trafford - 7/10 The young goalkeeper was kept busy throughout, making five saves to keep Spain at bay for large periods. While he could do little about the precision of the two late goals, his handling and command of the box under heavy pressure provided a solid foundation for the victory. Ezri Konsa - 8/10 A standout performance from the Arsenal defender, who showed great aerial prowess to score England’s second goal in the 53rd minute following a Declan Rice delivery. Defensively, he led the charts with a significant portion of England's 29 clearances, maintaining his composure as Spain flooded the box late on. Jarell Quansah - 7/10 Tasked with managing Oyarzabal, Quansah stood tall for much of the evening. He was vital in England's 20 interceptions, reading the game well and showing a maturity beyond his years in a high-stakes European encounter. Ben White - 8/10 White was exceptional on the right flank, balancing his defensive duties with a perfectly timed surge into the box to score England's third goal in the 57th minute. His contribution to the transition game was vital before his substitution. Lewis Hall - 6/10 A difficult evening at times for Hall, who had the unenviable task of tracking Lamine Yamal. While he struggled with Spain's overloads on the flank, he contributed to the defensive shape that limited Spain to just seven shots on target from 23 total attempts. His early yellow card in the 15th minute didn't deter his aggression, as he anchored the midfield brilliantly to disrupt Spain’s rhythm during their long spells of possession. item.title: England stun world champions Spain in one of their greatest victories
item.description: Anthony Gordon (from left), Jude Bellingham and Morgan Rogers celebrate a historic victory - Uefa via Getty Images/David Ramos Thomas Tuchel may not have planned it this way, but in one night he gave us all the rich history of the England team at once: some glorious attacking football, some self-sabotage defending, a red card, a late siege, and a fight. This was the beguiling story of Spain 2 England 3, an evening that began with the world champions parading the World Cup and ended with 10 Englishmen defending a lead with their last breath. England beat the world champions in Madrid, and for more than 30 minutes including injury time they did so with 10 men, Dan Burn heading the last ball out as per the tradition of a defensive rearguard action. This was the game that had it all: including a substitute, in Djed Spence, who had already picked up a yellow card on the bench before he came on. It was a coming-of-age performance in goal for James Trafford. So too for Ben White, the 2022 World Cup departee who scored the third and in the 84th minute lunged with astonishing effect to block a Nico Williams shot. Trafford again! 👊🏻An excellent double save from the Leeds United keeper 🙌 https://t.co/L27oQFQO1J — ITV Football (@itvfootball) November 15, 2026 This was a performance that was good enough to win a World Cup final, never mind Nations League A, Group 3 – just a shame England neglected to get to that final in the summer. The fight in question was at half-time as the players came off and White and Fabian Ruiz first tangled and others dived in. "There's a bit of a clash between the players"Tensions boil over as the two teams head down the tunnel for half-time. https://t.co/i7gqP1uTiU — ITV Football (@itvfootball) November 15, 2026 There was so much to enjoy. Harry Kane began the night as captain, scored his 93rd England goal from the spot and ended it coaching alongside Tuchel. Spain tried to grind out that last goal, but it never came. The Tuchel plan for the early stages – perhaps all stages – was a ferocious press against the best first-phase passing team in the world. Brave – but it worked beautifully and for an absorbing opening 10 minutes, Spain looked all at sea. Jude Bellingham and then Anthony Gordon both had chances to score. Unai Simón, the Spain captain for the start of the game, saved the first. The world champions had been waving the World Cup for the Madrid crowd just minutes earlier. That was right under the noses of the England team, waiting in line for the anthems and while not intended as a provocation it will certainly have not gone unnoticed by the visiting players. This Spain team were without Rodri, the world’s greatest controlling midfielder, and although he has a good replacement in Martín Zubimendi, the Arsenal man is nowhere near the level of the first choice. item.title: Mirra Andreeva issues strong message after winning the WTA Finals, ‘she is not getting the win’
item.description: Mirra Andreeva is your 2026 WTA Finals champion. The Russian youngster maintained her flawless status at the end-of-year event, beating Elina Svitolina 7-5, 6-3 in Sunday’s final. It was another superb performance by the young Russian, who has also defeated Aryna Sabalenka, Diana Shnaider and Jessica Pegula in the past week. Andreeva was particularly effective off the return, winning 52 per cent of all points off Svitolina’s first serve, as reported by Sofascore . Following Sunday’s contest, Andreeva was a picture of defiance. Mirra Andreeva reveals her embattled thought process after beating Elina Svitolina “It was the second time in my life where I just thought I am going to die on the court but she is not getting the win,” Andreeva told Sky Sports in the immediate aftermath of Sunday’s blockbuster. “I felt like if she wins today it is going to be over my dead body. I am going to have blisters, cramps, everything you can possibly have but I will not lose this match. “This spirit and fighting mindset helped me get through and get more brave and aggressive in important moments,” the 19-year-old concluded. Andreeva then commented on the intensity inside the Indian Wells Centre Court, before expressing her delight at claiming her first WTA Finals crown. “I felt in the first match we played against each other that she was lacking a bit of freedom but here I knew that the match would be tough. If she gained momentum she would play better,” Andreeva, who defeated Svitolina in the group stage, noted. “I felt like two of the longest games we had on her serve and my serve she won them. So we give her credit, as it was not like I was the only one winning the long points. Mirra Andreeva’s path to winning the 2026 WTA Finals Round robin: defeated Elina Svitolina 6-4, 6-0 Round robin: defeated Aryna Sabalenka 6-4, 6-0 Round robin: defeated Diana Shnaider 6-2, 6-1 Semi-finals: defeated Jessica Pegula 6-3, 6-4 Final: defeated Elina Svitolina 7-5, 6-3 “But I just tried to make her life super complicated and I was hoping that she would know even if she wins this long point or game she would have to work twice as hard to win the next one.” “This is a dream,” she added. “I had a little break down in my practice just before heading to Indian Wells as it would be the first time that I have played in singles. “I did not want to lose the match in the group and I did not lose a match at all. It is crazy, something unbelievable. I am going to celebrate, get a car!” Mirra Andreeva emulates Ashleigh Barty As per statisticians OptaAce, Andreeva has become the first player to win the WTA Finals in her maiden appearance at the event since Ashleigh Barty in 2019. Barty, a three-time major champion, ironically also defeated Elina Svitolina in the 2019 final. The Australian also beat Petra Kvitova, Belinda Bencic and Karolina Pliskova in Shenzhen, China. Photo by VCG/VCG via Getty Images Barty did not compete in another WTA Finals event before retiring from her playing career i

item.title: How England found a new edge to beat Spain and exorcise agony of Argentina defeat
item.description: England hold out, for a raucous win that will rightly be held up. Sure, it might not have been what it could have been as Ben White surged in for a sensational third in Madrid… but that last word remains key. England beat the world and European champions 3-2 in their own capital, to end the longest unbeaten run in international history, that stretched back to March 2024. Spain couldn’t make it 44 games, as England just about made it to 94 minutes. That was ultimately down to a brilliant double save from James Trafford, who was one of many positives on another Nations League night of enjoyably entertaining drama. Might Jordan Pickford ’s first place have gone with Spain’s unbeaten run? Trafford had to show his best. This was never going to be easy, no matter how Thomas Tuchel ’s side made it look for 63 minutes - until Elliott Anderson’s red card. That will be the manager’s main takeaway from the game, the “proof of concept” as he put it the night before. With 11 against 11, England were denying this Spanish team the ball and creating some swift chances that the world champions were struggling to live with. That was what the game-opening goal came from. Even if there was also debate about Anderson’s follow-through in that instance, England had opened another gap in the Spanish structure while looking so more cohesive and coruscating themselves. This is a team that can sustain attacking waves much better than the one who mostly forced their way through the summer on individual impact. White’s supreme goal, that had the world champions looking at each other and pointing fingers, was the grand exhibition of that. England celebrate a famous victory (Adam Davy/PA) (PA Wire) Just as crucially, it was so different to what Spain do. It was something of England's own. In between, Esri Konsa scored the plundered set-piece header that his recent performances have deserved. Jude Bellingham was at that point bossing the Spanish midfield, in the kind of way people have long imagined as his career has only escalated. This, and the very confidence from such a marker of a win, are what England have to take through to finally win that trophy at Euro 2028 . So many positives, so many solutions… until Spain asked the most severe questions, and Tuchel didn’t always have the answers. That is where there is obvious context to a win that should still inspire confidence. It clearly meant much more to England given the fact Spain are the world champions who had won at Wembley . They're the ones who have done it, the benchmark. Tuchel and all the players were aware they had to do something more, to close this year with a performance that offered more for the future; that they had to stand up. Harry Kane put England ahead from the spot (Adam Davy/PA) (PA Wire) They had admittedly felt frustration from that Wembley defeat; that they could have won. As a consequence, England just looked sharper for pretty much all of the first hour. Spain didn’t even have a shot on target in t

item.title: Memphis Tigers troll Louisville after wild comeback turns into total beatdown
item.description: Chris Day/The Commercial Appeal / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images Memphis Tigers troll Louisville after wild comeback turns into total beatdown appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Penny Hardaway and the Memphis Tigers earned a valuable win in non-conference action, blowing out the No. 10 Louisville Cardinals 98-78 on Sunday afternoon. Hardaway has been the Tigers’ head coach since 2018, going through his ninth season with the program. He is coming off his worst campaign last season, finishing 13-19 as injuries and inconsistent play summed up the 2025-26 season. Hardaway has determination to get his alma mater back on track, having led them to the NCAA Tournament three times. However, to get back to March Madness, they need wins over some of the best performing teams in the country. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) They got their wish against No. 10 Louisville, who they hosted on Sunday. Memphis had the upper hand, beating the brakes off the Cardinals in the second half of the contest. L’S DOWN Ⓜ️ #GoTigersGo pic.twitter.com/sZoNOx6XGN — Memphis Basketball (@Memphis_MBB) November 15, 2026 How Penny Hardaway, Memphis performed against Louisville Penny Hardaway and the Memphis Tigers will certainly garner votes for the next AP Top 25 poll, beating down Louisville in convincing fashion. It took some time for Memphis to get things going, struggling in the first half as Louisville led 54-41 at halftime. The Tigers exploded in the last 20 minutes of regulation, torching the Cardinals 57-26 as they locked in on both sides of the ball. Shot selection and free throws made the difference in this game. Memphis excelled by making 58% of their shots from the field and 80% from the free-throw line. It was the opposite for Louisville, only converting 44% of their chances and 57% at the charity stripe. Four players scored in double-digits for Memphis in the win. Jayden Reid led the squad with a stat line of 24 points, 10 assists, five rebounds, and four steals. He shot 8-of-16 from the field, including 1-of-4 from beyond the arc, and 7-of-7 from the free-throw line. Tylik Weeks came next with 24 points and five rebounds, Julius Thedford had 16 points and five rebounds, while Rihards Vavers provided 15 points and four rebounds. The Tigers will look forward to their next matchup, remaining at home. They host the Evansville Purple Aces as tip-off commences on Nov. 22 at 2 p.m. ET. item.title: When Arsenal Witnessed Dixie Dean Make Football History
item.description: When Arsenal Witnessed Dixie Dean Make Football History As many may or may not know, Highbury was a theatre when it came to all matters of sport, not only football, throughout its 93-year history (1913–2006). The grand old stage hosted football, cricket and boxing, but in terms of the beautiful game, it witnessed some of the most defining moments in footballing history. However, one of the greatest individual achievements involving Arsenal actually occurred away from the Gunners’ famous home, on the final day of the 1927/28 season, almost 100 years ago. Highbury would go on to become known as the “Home of Football” . The season proved to be nothing special for Arsenal, who were yet to embark on their “Golden Era” during the 1930s, when they lifted five league titles and two FA Cups. They finished far off from being title contenders that year. However, the man in charge was one of Arsenal’s most influential managers, Herbert Chapman, who laid the foundations for the North Londoners’ imminent future success, as well as changing the name of the closest tube station from Gillespie Road to Arsenal, amongst a number of revolutionary changes such as introducing white sleeves on the shirts during the early 1930s. His influence would eventually lead Arsenal to their first major trophy triumph in 1930 . Dixie Dean Faces Arsenal Chasing History On 5 May 1928, the Gunners travelled to Goodison Park to face Everton at their greatest, who had already been crowned league champions for the third time in their history prior to the famous game about to unfold. The official attendance was 48,715, although some accounts estimated that around 60,000 keen spectators were packed inside Goodison Park, waiting for history to be made. The Toffees featured arguably the greatest striker to ever play the game. His name was Dixie Dean, who only ever wanted to play for Everton after having been taken to watch the Merseysiders win the title during the 1914/15 season by his dad, before the football calendar was postponed for a few years due to the outbreak of the First World War. Dean was in search of breaking the English Football League record for the most goals scored in a season, which George Camsell had set with Middlesbrough not long beforehand, with 59 strikes in the Second Division before they were eventually promoted to the First Division in 1927. The only way he could set the bar was if he achieved an elusive hat-trick. The occasion also saw Arsenal legend Charlie Buchan make his final professional appearance before retiring from the game. Dean later suggested that Buchan showed little celebration of one of football’s most historic feats in the English game, perhaps feeling disappointed that Dixie’s record had overshadowed his own farewell. With the home and neutral fans hoping to see Dean open the scoresheet, they were met with instant disappointment after James Shaw broke the deadlock early on, beating the Everton goalkeeper to put Arsenal ahead. item.title: Andy Reid gives 5 injury updates after Chiefs’ big win
item.description: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - NOVEMBER 15: Jared Wiley #89 of the Kansas City Chiefs is carted off the field following an injury during the first quarter against the Atlanta Falcons at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on November 15, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs turned in a dominant performance against the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday, but the 60 minutes of winning football saw multiple injury scares early and often. On Kansas City’s first offensive possession, tight end Travis Kelce — who has been playing through an ankle injury — came up limping after making a 23-yard catch. While fans are used to seeing Kelce rest a moment on the sideline before reentering the game, this time the future Hall of Fame member was seen returning to the locker room with training staff. After Kansas City’s drive ended with a touchdown, the CBS broadcast showed fellow tight end Jared Wiley being carted back to the locker room. Kelce was ruled questionable and later returned. Wiley was almost immediately ruled out . Later in the first half, right guard Trey Smith went into concussion protocol. Smith too was later ruled out . Speaking after the game, head coach Andy Reid confirmed the worst news for Wiley. “As far as the injuries go, Wiley,” said Reid, “it looks like he fractured his ankle. That’s not a good one. Trey is in the concussion protocol. So, we’ll see where that goes. Kelce left for a bit with a calf. He’s been battling this ankle. It’s all kind of part of it there. He got landed on it on that first catch and twisted it up a little bit.” Smith’s return to action will require clearance from the team’s independent neuroglial consultant per the league’s concussion rules. Center Creed Humphrey had played every snap in 2026 until Week 9’s blowout win over the New York Jets firmly entered garbage time. Humphey briefly left the field in pain against Atlanta after a hand to the face. “Creed got poked in the eye,” Reid confirmed. Humphrey returned to play on the Chiefs’ next drive, and Reid showed no concern about his availability going forward. Rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane has battled a shoulder fracture the entire season. After breaking up a pass in the end zone, Delane was reported to be in pain and receiving aid from trainers. Delane missed Kansas City’s previous two games. Mansoor Delane is in pain on the Chiefs' bench. The trainers are heading his way. — Sam McDowell (@SamMcDowell11) November 15, 2026 Reid appeared confident that Delane avoided the worst case scenarios. “He landed on his back and kind of up in that shoulder area,” Reid remarked. “I think it sacred him more than anything. He’s going to be alright.” The Chiefs will welcome the Arizona Cardinals — now starting rookie quarterback Carson Beck — to Arrowhead Stadium in Week 11. item.title: The Chiefs’ offense rediscovers the deep ball in Atlanta
item.description: (Photo by Todd Kirkland/Getty Images) | Getty Images Leading into the Kansas City Chiefs ’ Week 10 bout with the Atlanta Falcons , quarterback Patrick Mahomes’ last deep-ball completion — a pass thrown 20 or more yards in the air — came in Week 4 against the Las Vegas Raiders . The recipient of the throw was wide receiver Tyquan Thornton, who dislocated his ankle on the play and was placed on the Reserve/Injured list. Between that play and Week 10, Mahomes completed none of his five downfield attempts. Poetically, the midseason trade for wide receiver Josh Downs was followed by Mahomes’ most prolific game of the year, with plenty of throws down the field. According to NFL Next Gen Stats , Mahomes completed three of six passes 20 or more yards downfield — each to a familiar face in the receiving corps. Rookie Cyrus Allen got open on a double-move down the left sideline for a 39-yard touchdown Veteran Rashee Rice came down with a 50-yard catch on a post route in traffic Training-camp standout Andrew Armstrong hauled in a long bomb in the end zone from a scrambling Mahomes It was Mahomes’ first game with multiple deep-pass touchdowns since 2021. It felt like his confidence throwing the long ball started with intermediate passes — including an 18-yard strike to Downs at the front pylon of the end zone. The back-shoulder touchdown is a rare sight in the Chiefs’ offense, but clearly, Downs has already earned enough respect from Mahomes to step up in the pocket and rifle the attempt there. After that pass put the Chiefs up 14-6, Mahomes kept challenging Atlanta’s coverage downfield and didn’t stop until the team was coasting to a late-fourth-quarter victory; he even threw a bomb to tight end Jake Briningstool into the end zone at one point. Downs may not be the target on these deep targets all the time, but it feels as if Mahomes needed a player like Downs to help establish a rhythm — and the rest of the receivers needed a player like Downs to relieve the pressure snap to snap.

item.title: Michigan Basketball Bombards William & Mary in Record-setting Performace
item.description: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Michigan will have to update its record books. After holding a mere five-point halftime lead, defending college basketball national champion Michigan exploded in the second half for 75 points on its way to a 123-79 win over William & Mary Saturday in Ann Arbor. It was the most points by Michigan in a single half in school history, and the most points in a game by the Wolverines since 1990. It also tied for fourth place on the all-time single-game scoring output list, matching the 123 points against Illinois-Chicago in 1986. “The season is going to deliver peaks and valleys, but I think the key is us having a holistic view of we want to be better today than a week ago. And I think we are,” Michigan first-year head coach Mike Boynton Jr. said. “If we continue that growth mindset then I don’t know what the ceiling of the team is, but I like the pieces and the ability of this team to find great success as they play more together and get guarded in different ways. “ Michigan (3-1) finished with eight players scoring in double figures – the most in school history. The Wolverines were led by true freshman forward Quinn Costello and transfer center Moustapha Thiam with 16 points each. Thiam also blocked four shots. Costello canned four 3-pointers and his final one snapped through the net with 5:59 left in the game to give Michigan 100 points and a 30-point lead. Also finishing in double figures were forward J.P. Estrella with 15, sophomore guard Trey McKenney with 14 and fifth-year guard Roddy Gayle Jr. with 13. Senior point guard Elliott Cadeua, junior forward Oscar Goodman and Kenny Noland scored 11 each. Cadeau also dished out 11 assists and made three steals. “So much is made about what last year’s team did, and that team went through a similar progression, and this team is going through its own evolution. I’m excited to see where it goes from here,” Boynton said. Michigan played a complete game in the second half and finished shooting 23-of-27 from the free throw line. William & Mary (2-2) was led by Stas Svika with 13 points and Brian Carter Jr. with 11. Michigan will travel to face Villanova on Saturday at 7 p.m. on FOX. The two teams met in the 2018 national championship game won by Villanova. Related Headlines J.J. item.description: ‘Time for You To Go,’ ‘Someone Needs To Be Fired’ — Packers Fans Turn the Heat on HC Matt LaFleur Following ‘Humbling’ Loss to Vikings Matt LaFleur called it a humbling experience. Plenty of Packers fans would like to know how many more of those they’re supposed to sit through. Green Bay’s loss to Minnesota brought another round of frustration, with fans calling for changes well beyond the next game plan. LaFleur’s postgame assessment did little to calm that crowd. For some, the familiar explanation was part of the problem. Packers Fans Have Heard Enough From Matt LaFleur The Vikings handed Green Bay a 30-10 defeat at Lambeau Field, completing a season sweep and dropping the Packers to 6-4. Minnesota improved to 7-2 behind Kirk Cousins, who threw two touchdown passes in his return to the Vikings. “This is a humbling league,” LaFleur said, according to The Athletic’s Matt Schneidman . That explanation landed about as well as the offense did. One supporter called on Packers president Ed Policy to make sweeping changes. “Policy needs to clean house. This hasn’t worked for 8 years,” the fan wrote . SET YOUR LINEUPS: PFN’s Free Fantasy Start/Sit Optimizer Those are demands from frustrated fans, with no indication in the supplied reporting that Green Bay has decided to make a coaching change. Still, the responses made clear how little patience those supporters had for another explanation after another divisional defeat. “When the [expletive] [are you] gonna stop being humbled??” another fan asked . Green Bay’s Performance Gives Critics Plenty To Work With The Packers supplied enough mistakes to keep the conversation going all week. Green Bay committed four turnovers, allowed eight sacks and finished with just 56 rushing yards. At halftime, the offense had managed 57 total yards while Minnesota built a 17-0 lead. Jordan Love sits 13th with a PFN QB Impact Score of 79.0 through 10 games. That broader evaluation offers some perspective on his season, but Sunday gave the offense very little to feel good about. item.title: CBS Inadvertently Roasts Colts CB Sauce Gardner After Embarrassing TD
item.description: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - DECEMBER 22: Sauce Gardner #1 of the Indianapolis Colts looks on prior to the game against the San Francisco 49ers at Lucas Oil Stadium on December 22, 2025 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) Getty The 2026 season has pretty much been a total nightmare for the Indianapolis Colts. The team is 2-7 entering Sunday’s game against the lowly Miami Dolphins and in the second quarter cornerback Sauce Gardner got absolutely roasted by the CBS graphic team, presumably on accident. The Dolphins employed a really nice trick play as the quarterback threw laterally to wide receiver Malik Washington and the Colts completely took the bait, moving up to try and make a tackle which allowed Jalen Tolbert to get wide open in the end zone for a very easy touchdown. The Colts player who was really responsible for the Dolphins scoring was probably either safety Cam Bynum or safety A.J. Haulcy as they both allowed Tolbert to easily get over the top, but as Haulcy ran off the field CBS flashed a graphic that said “Touchdown Sauce Gardner” which made it seem like Gardner got torched so bad on the play that he deserved credit for the touchdown. Ironically, if you watch the play Gardner is hardly even involved. He is on the far side of the field wearing No. 1 and really could not have had any sort of impact on the play even if he sprinted straight backwards towards the end zone right when the ball was snapped. You can see Gardner following Washington as he goes in motion to receive the lateral pass, but there was nothing he could have done. Still, it just speaks to the way things have gone for the Colts this season and how bad the Gardner trade looks a year later. Indianapolis traded for Gardner last November ahead of the trade deadline and gave the New York Jets two first-round picks and wide receiver Adonai Mitchell in the trade. Colts look foolish for the Sauce Gardner trade a year later The Colts were the inverse of what they are this season as they were 7-2 and looked to be one of the better teams in the AFC. The hope was that the trade would take them to the next level and give them a shutdown corner, but that is not how it has worked out. Gardner was one of the best corners in the NFL his first two seasons in the league but has not been the same guy in recent years. He still only has three career interceptions and does not have a pick with the Colts yet as his number of pass deflections has also gone down. That trade just looks worse and worse especially for a Colts team that is now very clearly in a state of quasi-rebuild after trading several players away in the last month. Gardner may not have deserved that graphic for the trick play from Miami, but maybe whoever pressed the wrong button on the CBS graphic crew was in some way trying to remind Colts fans just how bad an idea it was to get Gardner for that much. item.title: Why Italy will be top seeds in EURO 2028 qualifying draw
item.description: Why Italy will be top seeds in EURO 2028 qualifying draw Italy did not reach the Nations League quarter-finals, but there is still some good news, as they will be top seeds in the EURO 2028 qualifying campaign draw as one of the best third-placed teams. Roberto Mancini said when he first took the job over the summer that his primary focus was getting the Nazionale ready for the European Championships. The Nations League was a rollercoaster, going from a 2-0 opening home defeat to Belgium, through victories over Turkiye, a 1-1 draw in Paris, and historic 3-1 home win against Zinedine Zidane’s France on Thursday. They only needed a point in Brussels to go through to the quarter-finals, but were crushed 4-1 by the Red Devils . Italy will be top seeds in EURO 2028 draw BRUSSELS, BELGIUM – NOVEMBER 15: Jeremy Doku of Belgium and Michael Kayode of Italy battle for possession during the UEFA Nations League 2026/27 group phase match between Belgium and Italy at King Baudouin Stadium on November 15, 2026 in Brussels, Belgium. (Photo by Dean Mouhtaropoulos/Getty Images) The good news is, although Italy finished third in Group A1, they are one of the best to miss out on the quarter-finals with 10 points. That means they will be they will certainly avoid the play-offs for Nations League relegation, and will be among the 12 top seeds for the EURO 2028 qualifying draw. That is going to be held on December 6 in Belfast. BRUSSELS, BELGIUM – NOVEMBER 15: Roberto Mancini, Head Coach of Italy, looks on during the UEFA Nations League 2026/27 group phase match between Belgium and Italy at King Baudouin Stadium on November 15, 2026 in Brussels, Belgium. (Photo by Dean Mouhtaropoulos/Getty Images) What does remain to be seen is whether the Azzurri will be in a group with four or five nations. Those qualifiers will be played between March and November 2027.

item.title: England End Spain’s 44-Game Unbeaten Run With Nations League Win
item.description: England snapped world champions Spain’s unbeaten run with a 3-2 victory in Madrid on Sunday to clinch the top spot in Nations League group A3. Goals from Harry Kane, Ezri Konsa and Ben White inflicted La Roja’s first loss in a competitive game since March 2023, after 44 without defeat. England’s Elliot Anderson was sent off in the second half as Spain fought back from three goals down with strikes from Mikel Oyarzabal and Nico Williams, but Luis de la Fuente’s World Cup winners could not find the equaliser. Both sides were already sure to progress, but as group winners England will be seeded for the quarter-finals in March. England coach Thomas Tuchel selected James Trafford in goal over Jordan Pickford and also brought White and Konsa into the side. Teenage star Lamine Yamal was fit to start for Spain at Atletico Madrid’s Metropolitano stadium after missing their midweek win over the Czech Republic. However the youngster did not see much of the ball in the first half as England came out strongly. Spain’s midfielder #09 Fermin Lopez challenges England’s goalkeeper #13 James Trafford during the UEFA Nations League – League A day 6 group 3 – football match between Spain and England at Metropolitano Stadium in Madrid on November 15, 2026. (Photo by Thomas COEX / AFP) Spain goalkeeper Unai Simon produced a strong reaction save to deny Jude Bellingham, while Anthony Gordon had a dangerous shot blocked. Ballon d’Or winner Kane, who beat Yamal to the award, sent an effort narrowly wide. Barcelona defender Pau Cubarsi handed England the advantage when he clumsily felled Kane in the area on the stroke of half time. The Bayern Munich hitman powered a perfect penalty past Simon, who dived the right way but to no avail. De la Fuente tried to react at half-time with a triple change, including throwing on Barcelona duo Fermin Lopez and Pedri, but England quickly found more joy. England’s midfielder #17 Morgan Rogers fights for the ball with Spain’s forward #17 Nico Williams during the UEFA Nations League – League A day 6 group 3 – football match between Spain and England at Metropolitano Stadium in Madrid on November 15, 2026. (Photo by Javier SORIANO / AFP) Konsa headed home the second from Declan Rice’s corner in the 53rd minute after the Arsenal defender was left unmarked by Spain’s defence. Four minutes later England sliced open Spain’s defence with Kane and Bellingham combining to set up White for the third. La Roja clawed their way back into the game when Elliot Anderson fouled Yamal in the area as the Spain striker ran in on goal. The Manchester City midfielder was dismissed and Mikel Oyarzabal slotted home the penalty. Spain found a second when Gordon gave the ball away and Yamal fed Nico Williams, whose shot hit the post and bounced in. Williams curled over and Trafford denied Yamal and Marc Cucurella as Spain looked fruitlessly for the goal they needed to preserve their unbeaten record. item.title: 2027: Soludo urges politicians to keep off places of worship
item.description: Gov. Chukwuma Soludo of Anambra has urged politicians to keep politics away from places of worship, saying religious institutions should remain centres of spiritual growth and unity. Soludo made the call during a visit to the Mountain of Holy Ghost Intervention Deliverance Ministry Inc., Onitsha, to celebrate its 30th anniversary. The ministry was founded by Prophet Chukwuemeka Ohanaemere, popularly known as Odumeje. He said: “Politicians, keep off places of worship! I do not do politics in the house of God. “I deliberately avoided church campaigns for six months before the last governorship election in Anambra. “My visit to religious institutions is usually motivated by my commitment to ecumenism and responsibility as the father of all in the state”. The governor described the anniversary as a significant milestone, noting that it marked maturity, preparation and a new phase in the ministry’s growth. He recalled that his first encounter with the ministry was during the demolition of part of its structure by the state government to facilitate the dredging of the Sakamori drainage channel. Soludo commended Odumeje for his contributions to charity and efforts towards societal development. He also acknowledged the cleric’s support for the state’s campaign against criminal idolatry and activities of illegal traditional spiritual practitioners. According to him, the advocacy, alongside the Anambra Homeland Security Law, has contributed to making the state safer. Responding, Odumeje pledged continued partnership with the state government to drive progress and development. item.title: Disu assures Abia residents of improved security
item.description: By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — The Inspector-General of Police (IGP), Olatunji Disu, has assured residents of Abia State of improved security, pledging that the Nigeria Police Force would intensify efforts to protect lives and property across the state. Disu gave the assurance during a courtesy visit to Governor Alex Otti at Government House, Umuahia, where he commended the governor for his sustained support to the police. The IGP, who said he had received positive reports from the Commissioner of Police and the Assistant Inspector-General of Police on the state government’s assistance to the Force, promised that the police would reciprocate the gesture through improved service delivery. “I want to thank you for all you have been doing for my officers. My Commissioner of Police has told me all you have been doing for us. The AIG too reiterated it. Thank you so much for it,” Disu said. He assured the governor that the police would remain committed to tackling security challenges and ensuring the safety of residents. “I will give you my word that we will continue to do our best to ensure proper policing so that people of the state will be able to sleep with their two eyes closed,” he said. Disu explained that his visit to Abia was primarily to attend the traditional marriage ceremony of his orderly, Victor Nnah Sunday, at Amangwu, Abaki-Ndoki, in Ukwa East Local Government Area. He, however, said he considered it necessary to pay homage to Otti, as the state’s Chief Security Officer, before proceeding to the wedding venue. Responding, Otti commended the police leadership for its professionalism and prompt response to the state government’s requests for assistance in addressing security challenges. “Thank you for what you do for the country. Thank you for the professionalism of the Force and for making everyone realise that the safety and security of the people is paramount. “We have had instances where we called upon you and you responded swiftly,” the governor said. Otti also praised the promotion of the immediate past Commissioner of Police in Abia to the rank of Assistant Inspector-General of Police, describing his service in the state as professional and tactful. He said the former police commissioner demonstrated commitment in handling security matters, adding that although the state would have preferred to retain him, his elevation was a welcome development. “He demonstrated professionalism and tact in the discharge of his duties. If not that it is a promotion, we would have resisted it, but we believe it is good for him to move on,” Otti said. The governor expressed optimism that the officer would sustain his relationship with Abia despite his new position. Otti also congratulated the IGP’s orderly on his traditional marriage, recalling that he had met him during an earlier encounter with the police chief. item.title: 2027: Atiku promises to end insecurity if elected
item.description: By Nabilu Balarabe The Presidential candidate of African Democratic Congress (ADC), Atiku Abubakar has promised to tackle insurgency and other forms of insecurity, if voted in the 2027 Presidential election. Atiku made the promise in Potiskum on Sunday during the party’s campaign rally. He also promised to provide an enabling environment for youths to develop careers in all areas of their interest. “Whatever you want to do, my administration will support you. But we will not allow all acts of violence,” he said. Abubakar said he would revive the economy by providing affordable fuel, electricity and cutting taxes. He, however, said all these could only be achieved if voters came out en-mass to vote for him in the forthcoming election. Abubakar advised the electorate to vote wisely for candidates that would better their lot and reject corrupt and selfish politicians. “Vote the ADC for your future and the future of your children. We are ready to serve you in every way we can,” Atiku said. In his remarks, the ADC National Secretary, Mr Rauf Aregbesola, thanked the people of Yobe for their warm reception to the party’s candidates. He urged the electorate to vote for change and ensure that due process was followed in counting and collation of votes cast. item.title: One firefighter injured as hoodlums attack crew in Abuja
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA — One firefighter was injured after suspected hoodlums attacked a Federal Fire Service crew responding to a fire emergency at 7th Avenue, Gwarinpa, Abuja, at the weekend. The suspected perpetrators have reportedly been arrested and are under investigation following the incident. The Federal Capital Territory Command of the service condemned the attack in a statement issued by its Public Relations Officer, Superintendent of Fire Anyam Barnabas. The statement said the firefighters, attached to the Kubwa Metropolitan Fire Station, were responding to a distress call from a resident, Mrs Amina, at about 10am when they came under attack. On arrival at the scene, the crew were reportedly pelted with stones by suspected hoodlums, leaving one firefighter injured. The injured officer was immediately taken to a hospital for medical attention. The incident was reported to the Galadima Police Station, while the suspects were said to be under investigation. The Controller of the Federal Fire Service, FCT Command, Mohammed Anas, expressed displeasure over what he described as persistent attacks on firefighters while carrying out their statutory responsibilities. He warned that anyone who attacked or obstructed firefighters at emergency scenes would face the consequences of the law. Anas urged residents of the FCT to appreciate and support firefighters, particularly during emergency operations, and called on those involved in such acts to desist. He reaffirmed the command’s commitment to prompt and effective emergency response across the territory, stressing that firefighters must be allowed to perform their duties without intimidation, harassment or attacks. The controller also appealed to residents to cooperate with emergency responders and provide the necessary support to enable them to save lives and protect property. The post One firefighter injured as hoodlums attack crew in Abuja appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Igbokoda Crash: NAF recovers black box, holds memorial November 26
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Nigerian Air Force (NAF) has confirmed the recovery of the Cockpit Voice Recorder (CVR) from the site of the October 5 aircraft crash at Igbokoda, Ondo State, announcing plans to hold a memorial service and wreath-laying ceremony for the victims on November 26. The ceremony will take place at the National Military Cemetery, Abuja, in honour of the personnel and other victims who lost their lives in the NAF 931 aircraft accident. NAF Director of Public Relations and Information, Air Commodore Ehimen Ejodame, disclosed this in a statement on Sunday, saying the event would provide an opportunity for bereaved families, colleagues, friends and members of the Air Force community to pay their last respects. He said the ceremony would also serve as a formal expression of the Service’s respect and remembrance for those who died in the incident. On the recovery of the aircraft’s black box, Ejodame said the CVR, alongside other aircraft fragments and relevant evidence, had been retrieved from the crash site. He explained that data recovered from the voice recorder was being analysed and was expected to contribute significantly to the ongoing investigation into the circumstances surrounding the accident. According to him, the investigation is progressing in collaboration with the Nigerian Safety Investigation Bureau (NSIB) and the Nigerian Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA). The Air Force reiterated its commitment to ensuring that the investigation was conducted in accordance with the highest standards of professionalism, transparency, accountability and responsibility, while supporting the independent technical processes required to establish the cause of the crash. Ejodame further disclosed that recovery operations had yielded several human remains and aircraft fragments, while the identification process for the recovered remains was ongoing. He said the operation had been particularly challenging because of the swampy nature of the terrain and the depth to which some of the aircraft wreckage had penetrated the ground. The NAF spokesman added that the Service was engaging relevant agencies to address environmental concerns arising from the recovery exercise and ensure appropriate remediation after its completion. He said the Air Force recognised the grief of the bereaved families and remained committed to providing them with sustained support throughout the difficult period. The Service also appreciated the cooperation of relevant agencies, host communities and other stakeholders who had continued to support the recovery and investigation efforts. The NAF assured the public of its commitment to a thorough investigation, responsible environmental management and the dignified remembrance of all those who lost their lives. item.title: Sanusi, Ladoja warn against politicising traditional institutions
item.description: By Adeola Badru The Emir of Kano, Muhammadu Sanusi II, and the Olubadan of Ibadanland, Oba Rashidi Ladoja, have called for national healing, peaceful coexistence and stronger bonds among Nigeria’s diverse ethnic and religious groups, warning against the politicisation of traditional institutions. The two traditional rulers spoke on Sunday in Ibadan when Sanusi paid a courtesy visit to Ladoja at his palace in Oke-Aremo, where they stressed the need for traditional institutions to remain above partisan interests and serve as instruments of reconciliation, mutual understanding and national unity. Sanusi, who was in Ibadan to honour an invitation from the League of Imams and Alfas in South-West Nigeria, said his visit reflected his belief in a country where ethnic, religious and political differences would not determine relationships among citizens. He described the engagement as one of the positive developments needed to bridge Nigeria’s regional and cultural divides, stressing that national unity, progress and prosperity could only be achieved when people from different backgrounds deliberately reached out to one another. The Emir said although other engagements had emerged, he considered it important to honour his earlier commitment to attend the conference, even if his participation would be brief. “We fixed this date a long time ago, and even though other events came, we considered it important to honour our promise to appear at the conference, even if it is for a brief period, because they have been expecting me to come. “This invitation is part of the positive developments we have been yearning for to build a bridge where Nigerians from different parts of the country reach out to each other and come together in the interest of the unity, the progress and the prosperity of our dear nation,” he said. Sanusi also apologised for the delay in visiting Ladoja following his appointment and coronation, explaining that certain circumstances had prevented him from attending earlier. He congratulated Ladoja on his ascension to the throne of his forebears and prayed for divine protection, a long and peaceful reign, as well as prosperity for Ibadanland and Nigeria. The Emir described the courtesy visit as necessary, given the longstanding relationship between the two traditional institutions and their respective communities. Reflecting on his relationship with Ibadan, Sanusi recalled his longstanding connections with the ancient city dating back to his days at First Bank, his association with the late Aare Musulumi of Yorubaland, Alhaji Abdulazeez Arisekola Alao, and his subsequent tenure as Governor of the Central Bank of Nigeria. He said Ibadan had remained a familiar destination over the years, adding that he had maintained close relationships with several indigenes of the city. Sanusi also expressed his readiness to host the Olubadan in Kano, saying reciprocal visits would further strengthen the longstanding bonds between the two communities and promot

item.title: NDC candidate in Kwara pledges N120,000 minimum wage for workers
item.description: The governorship candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in Kwara, Prof. Abdulmumin Ajia, has pledged a minimum wage of N120,000 for workers in the state. Ajia made the pledge on Sunday in Ilorin while unveiling the NDC’s 2027 Gubernatorial Campaign Council manifesto, tagged ‘Forward Kwara Agenda’. He proposed a N120,000 public-service minimum wage benchmark and a cost-of-living adjustment framework for workers and pensioners. He said his administration would verify the payroll, assess the financial implications, consult labour unions and publish an implementation and funding timetable. On pensioners, Ajia promised to verify outstanding gratuities and publish a schedule for settling validated arrears. He also pledged to establish a predictable payment timetable for newly due pension obligations. Ajia said he entered the governorship race to make public institutions work reliably for all Kwarans, regardless of political affiliation. “I am running to make public institutions work that way. If entrusted with office, I will serve people who support me, people who oppose me and people who have never attended a political meeting,” he said. He said his experience as a teacher, researcher and university administrator had taught him to ask critical questions, examine evidence and take responsibility for results. Ajia, who led a School of Business and mentored young people, said his visits home exposed him to the challenges facing unemployed graduates. He said many young people could hardly predict when fair employment opportunities would become available. According to him, government has a responsibility to ensure that citizens understand how to access assistance, eligibility requirements and appeal procedures. He said access to public services should not depend on personal relationships with the governor. Ajia said the Forward Kwara Agenda outlined six areas of governance, anchored on stronger institutions, greater opportunities and shared prosperity. On security, he said farmers should access their farms, children should travel safely to school and traders should return home safely from markets. NAN reports that the event attracted hundreds of NDC stakeholders from the state’s 16 local government areas. The post NDC candidate in Kwara pledges N120,000 minimum wage for workers appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: ‘Xavi wants to play Xavi-style football’ – Klopp praises Netherlands coach
item.description: Germany coach Jurgen Klopp praised Xavi Hernandez on Sunday, saying the new Netherlands coach already had the Dutch playing in his own image after just five games in charge. Speaking in Berlin ahead of Monday’s meeting between the two old rivals, Klopp pointed to Friday’s 7-0 thumping of Greece in Amsterdam and said the former midfielder had made an impression. Considered among the best midfielders in the history of the game, Xavi formed the core of a possession-dominant Barcelona side who won four Champions League titles. He also won the World Cup with Spain. “They simply played some electric football,” Klopp said, adding: “Xavi wants to play Xavi-style football… “He’s a coach who really pushes his approach to the limit. And that’s exciting. I always loved playing against teams who play like this.” Third in the group with only the top two reaching the quarter-finals, Germany will need to beat the Netherlands to give themselves a chance. “They’re a team who really come alive in European football,” Klopp said of the Netherlands. “It’s one of the fiercest rivalries in football. It’s a great honour for me.” Appointed in August, the Spaniard said he was beginning to understand the nature of the rivalry with Germany. “Now I can understand more because I’m here and I feel this kind of rivalry. It will be a really good test for us,” Xavi said. In his press conference, Xavi deflected Klopp’s praise and said the Netherlands’ big win over Greece was down to his players. “It’s not Xavi-football. It’s all about the players. They are the most important. I don’t need to convince them to play this style of football, they have the capacity to play like the last game. Germany and the Netherlands played out a 1-1 draw in Amsterdam in September, the first match in charge for both Klopp and Xavi. Xavi said he would try and do the unexpected on Monday, but acknowledged it would not be easy against the former Liverpool and Borussia Dortmund coach. “It’s difficult to surprise a coach like Jurgen Klopp,” Xavi said. “He’s one of the best coaches in the past few years. And it’s an honour to come up against him tomorrow.” Vanguard News The post ‘Xavi wants to play Xavi-style football’ – Klopp praises Netherlands coach appeared first on Vanguard News .
